static_traits.name: Wang Wendy
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems in the past; not yet received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, good cooperation; can describe automatic thoughts and trigger situations specifically; tone neutral to cautious; tending to use self-reproaching language like 'should' and 'must'

basic_info.main_problem: I especially feel incompetent and not good enough in terms of faith; this feeling worsened after encountering challenges at work and in personal life, and gradually spread to all aspects of life.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize the sense of incompetence has affected my daily functioning and overall well-being, prompting me to seek counseling.
growth_experiences: Wendy Wang's father once worked at Microsoft, with remarkable career achievements. Wendy Wang has continuously compared herself against her father's success while growing up and as an adult; in recent months, under work pressure and personal life challenges, such comparisons intensified, triggering and reinforcing her self-doubt and sense of incompetence.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough (unable to become a competent employee or a devout believer)

special_situations.event: In an urgent work project, not yet able to complete deadline tasks on time
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot complete tasks on time, it means I am very incompetent, and may even lose my job because of it
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Not resting, forcing work forward to make up for mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am very incompetent; I may lose my job because of it

special_situations.event: Unable to focus during prayer or Bible study, or performing poorly when participating in religious activities and discussions
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot focus and meet standards in faith practice, it means I am a bad person or not devout
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Attending church more frequently, seeking advice from friends to correct inadequacies (though not yet effective)
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot even keep up with my own faith; I am a bad person

special_situations.event: Comparing my own professional performance with my father's success at Microsoft
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach father's level of success, it proves I am inferior and simply not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forces self with harsh self-criticism and higher standards
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never be as good as him; I am simply not good enough

special_situations.event: The project was eventually completed but still could not meet the ideal standards or the original timeline
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only fully meeting the best standard and being on time counts as success; otherwise it is failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly reviewing and criticizing oneself afterward, denying existing achievements
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This does not count as success; I should have done better and faster

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and accepted, wanting to be seen as a capable professional and a devout believer
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged as not good enough, being negated, or being seen as not devout, even worrying about losing work and interpersonal support because of it
defense_goal: Controls failure risk through self-harshness and raising standards
Avoiding revealing specific feelings to friends to reduce the discomfort of exposing vulnerability

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough daughter, employee, and believer (prone to failure, needing to work harder just to barely qualify)
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh judges (the father figure, superiors, or religious groups will scrutinize and criticize with high standards)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When missing work deadlines or being unable to focus in religious practice
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others will think I am incompetent or not devout; my inadequacies will be exposed
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Quickly blaming oneself in a low tone, frequently using 'should/must' constructions, shortening answers, reducing detail disclosure, avoiding seeking external support.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When comparing oneself with the father's career achievements or thinking of the high standards outside
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: I must meet external standards to be valuable; otherwise I am a failure
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing external standards as absolute truth, repeatedly using 'I must / I should', belittling one's own achievements and demanding higher goals.

manifestations: Tense relationships with friends, but not yet discussed specific feelings with them
Feeling not good enough in the religious community due to self-judgment, finding it hard to engage
outcomes: Persistent self-doubt and sense of incompetence
Avoiding deep communication leading to insufficient support

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Internalizing the high standards of father and religious groups as one's self-measuring yardstick

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Self-blame of the 'I should have done better' type
Not yet discussed specific feelings with close friends; overly cautious and self-restricting

positive_force: Still able to complete work projects (albeit delayed) and experience partial relief (such as the lightness after completion)
Proactively seeking professional counseling, maintaining a certain hope and willingness to change
Has some religious participation foundation (continuously attends church)
Has a few close friends as potential support resources
negative_force: Long-term self-comparison (using father's success as reference) leading to inferiority and negation
Black-and-white and positive-negating cognitive patterns, solidifying the sense of incompetence
Strong self-blame and 'should' statements, reducing self-compassion and flexibility
Not discussing specific feelings with friends, reducing external support and corrective feedback

target_behavior.behavior: Intense self-blame and anxiety when making work mistakes or being unable to focus in religious activities, accompanied by repeated negative self-talk (e.g. 'I am very incompetent', 'I am a bad person')
antecedent: A sudden change in project scope and team member absences causing the task to be blocked
Attention not focused during prayer or Bible study
Feeling one's performance is lacking during religious discussions
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjective evaluation using father's high achievements and religion's high standards as reference, triggering black-and-white and positive-negating cognitive biases, leading to doubting self-efficacy and worth.
target_behavior.function: Trying to avoid external judgment through self-criticism and high demands, maintaining a sense of control and driving self-improvement (avoidance and self-punishment as negative reinforcement).
target_behavior.consequence: Work performance affected, interpersonal tension, decreased religious participation and increased guilt, overall well-being reduced.
